work.permit: work permit from the Department of Labor and Employment

note: Read 2026-10-31 on the Lawphil Project (Arellano Law Foundation), which publishes the Acts' texts as enacted; the Official Gazette's site answered with a Cloudflare challenge. Majority: Republic Act No. 6809 (1989), amending the Family Code, art. 234: majority commences at eighteen, which emancipates (art. 236, not read: an emancipated person is qualified for all acts of civil life, save marriage consent under twenty-one). Work: Republic Act No. 9231 (2003), s. 2, amending s. 12 of RA 7610: children below fifteen may not be employed, save two exceptions; from fifteen to seventeen work is allowed outside hazardous work and within hours limits (no work from 10 pm to 6 am; not held). Exception 1, work in a family enterprise under the parents' sole responsibility, isn't held. Performers: exception 2: a child below fifteen may be employed in public entertainment or information through cinema, theatre, radio, television or other media where the participation is essential, on a contract the parents conclude, with the child's agreement where possible and the Department of Labor and Employment's approval; the employer must first secure a work permit from the Department (the 'Working Child Permit'). Below fifteen: at most twenty hours a week, none between 8 pm and 6 am (not held); a trust fund of 30% of earnings above P200,000 a year (not held). No lowest age. Service: Service is held null: no source saying no service is asked was reached today (the blocker file names the attempts); a reading only, not held: there is no conscription (the National Service Training Program, RA 9163, is a college course; not read).

sources.title: Republic Act No. 6809 (1989), Lawphil Project
sources.said: AN ACT LOWERING THE AGE OF MAJORITY FROM TWENTY-ONE TO EIGHTEEN YEARS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ... Emancipation takes place by the attainment of majority. Unless otherwise provided, majority commences at the age of eighteen years.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 9231 (2003), Lawphil Project
sources.said: Children below fifteen (15) years of age shall not be employed except: ... Where a child's employment or participation in public entertainment or information through cinema, theater, radio, television or other forms of media is essential: ... the employer shall first secure, before engaging such child, a work permit from the Department of Labor and Employment which shall ensure observance of the above requirements.
